Spotlight: Merely ninth of 19 in the King George V Stakes at Royal Ascot (1m4f, good to firm) but he failed to settle and prior to that he kept on for a good third in the London Gold Cup at Newbury (1m2f, good) on his handicap and seasonal debut, shaping as though 1m4f could be right up his street; retains potential at this trip and could be a contender if settling better.

OwnerName: Al Shaqab Racing & Stall Perlen AB
Spotlight: Runner-up to notable rivals on first two starts before winning 1m4f maiden at Leopardstown (good) in May; well beaten when favourite on handicap debut in the King George V Stakes at Royal Ascot (1m4f, good to firm) but he raced in the rear and things didn't go his way tactically; Irish stable won this last year and he might be worth another chance.

Won 1m2f maiden at Pontefract (1m2f, good) in April on third start and he was third on recent handicap debut at Chester (10.3f, good) where not much went right, as he was slowly away, failed to settle and denied a clear run before staying on strongly; this close relation to Group 1 winner Nezwaah could be quite a bit better than his current mark, especially now at 1m4f.

Won at Nottingham (1m2f, good) in April on second start and runner-up in novice there (1m2f, good to soft) in May when last seen; he's not obviously well treated off his opening mark but this 220,000gns yearling is bred to be suited by 1m4f and is open to further improvement; wears a first-time tongue-tie; one to watch in the betting.

Runner-up twice in a row (1m2f, good; including behind Bay Royale) before showing improved form for the step up in trip and getting off the mark at the fifth attempt in a novice at Doncaster (1m4f, good to firm) three weeks ago; he was impressive last time and is just the type of 3yo from this yard to keep on progressing; firmly in calculations on handicap debut.

Third of 14 on handicap debut at York (1m4f, good) in May and the form of his subsequent second of four at Wolverhampton (1m4f, AW) has worked out well; sold out of George Boughey's yard for £170,000 last month and he's in with an each-way shout on this first run for Ian Williams.

Capitalised on a reduced mark at Thirsk (1m4f, good to firm) on July 1 and he followed up at Newmarket (1m4f, good to firm) ten days later; clearly in good heart but those wins came in five-runner, Class 4 handicaps and this is a much sterner test of his credentials.

Beaten just a neck at Pontefract (1m4f, good) last month on his second start before 5l fourth of eight to Hatteen at Doncaster (1m4f, good to firm); he's 8lb better off with the winner for this handicap debut and further improvement is possible, but it's needed in this warm contest and there's a suspicion he may appreciate a longer trip.

RaceName: Racing TV Free Trial British Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Ran poorly when favourite for a C&D handicap in May; in good form prior to that and a return to form would come as no surprise; high on the list.

RaceName: Racing TV Free Trial British Apprentice Handicap
OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Disappointed at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) 33 days ago; earlier Windsor third was a solid effort though and the return of blinkers (worn at Windsor but left off latest) could see him resume his progress.

RaceName: Racing TV Free Trial British Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Ran his best race of the year when third of eight at Chepstow (6f, good to firm) 26 days ago, his first run after a gelding operation; regular slow starts aren't ideal and the switch to blinkers isn't enough to earn him the vote.

RaceName: Racing TV Free Trial British Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Had a fine year in 2025, winning five times; in and out this year but his latest York second (of 19) was a fine run and he needs serious consideration despite a 3lb rise.

RaceName: Racing TV Free Trial British Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Still seeking a first handicap success; huge chance on his 2024 form but he went the wrong way last season and his return to action at Doncaster last month was uninspiring; he has had a wind operation, his second, since but there are risks attached.

RaceName: Racing TV Free Trial British Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Not the force of old but that is reflected in his mark; had wind surgery prior to York 18 days ago, a race in which he ran with more promise than his finishing position suggests; dropped 3lb and the return of headgear can help; better run can be expected.

RaceName: Racing TV Free Trial British Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Conditions to suit and he ran his best race of the year when third over C&D in May; beaten twice since but he is being given a chance by the handicapper.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Alice Keppel Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: The door opened on her fifth start when landing Hamilton maiden (5f) in June and she showed improved form to romp away with three-runner nursery over that C&D (also good to firm; made all) a fortnight ago; this is much tougher but she's putting it together and might get them at it.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Alice Keppel Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Really promising debut when bustling up an odds-on shot at York (good) last month but she wasn't overly impressive when justifying short odds at Windsor (also 5f, good to firm) a fortnight later; will need to better that effort but it's still very early days.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Alice Keppel Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Made virtually all when she took a Windsor novice (5f, good to firm; first-time blinkers) with authority at the start of last month; those tactics were always going to be hard to pull off when 150-1 and down the field in the Queen Mary 16 days later but they will be better deployed at this venue, albeit pace pressure looks likely.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Alice Keppel Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Solid third on her debut over C&D in May and her narrow second at Nottingham next time has been well advertised by the winner subsequently; midfield in the Group 2 Queen Mary last month but made no mistake when effortlessly taking Beverley novice (5f, good to firm; first-time tongue-tie) a fortnight ago; yard could hardly be in better form; respected.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Alice Keppel Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Caught the eye when second on her debut at Ripon (5f, good) near the start of last month and it was a fine effort from the front when fifth in the Group 3 Albany (6f, good to firm) two weeks later; appeared to find the latter trip a stretch and today's drop back to 5f looks a good move.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Alice Keppel Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Narrowly opened her account when taking AW maiden (6f) in May; she's fine on turf and posted good efforts in a French Listed race and the Queen Mary (head behind Wild Blossom) at Royal Ascot before respectable third in Sandown Listed event (5f, good) four weeks ago; that latest form has taken a few knocks but she can't be ruled out.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Alice Keppel Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: All starts at 5f; a commanding win on her debut at Beverley (good to soft; made all) in April promised plenty but she's not really kicked on; fairly close third in Sandown Listed event in May was potentially a run to build on but she weakened to be beaten about 10l in the Queen Mary last time; Ryan Moore takes the reins and this filly is not discounted if tapping back into that initial promise.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Alice Keppel Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Stormed home to win by 10l on her debut at Carlisle (good) in May but she couldn't produce similar fireworks in the Queen Mary (also 5f, good to firm) last time; however, she was still beaten only about 4l that day in what looked a good renewal; the pick of James Doyle and she's a player.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Alice Keppel Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: She got off the mark over 6f at Yarmouth in June and was up late to bag a valuable sales race at Newbury (good to firm) when dropped to 5f 11 days ago; this easier 5f isn't sure to suit but a solid pace looks likely, which will help, and she's progressing.

RaceName: Start Your Racing TV Free Trial Apprentice Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Fourth foal; half-sister to bumper winner Cut The Rope; she would be an unlikely winner on debut.

RaceName: Start Your Racing TV Free Trial Apprentice Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Made a winning debut at Newmarket (7f, good to firm; blinkered; 7lb worse off with runner-up Areti today) last month; no match for the odds-on favourite at Salisbury (7f, good to firm) 18 days ago but she finished clear of the third; solid form claims.

RaceName: Start Your Racing TV Free Trial Apprentice Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Ninth foal; half-sister to winners Hathfa (5f AW; RPR 71) and Yardan (French 7.5f/Qatari 1m); dam unraced half-sister to 6f 2yo Group 1 winner Shalaa; has a fair standard to aim at on debut but worth a market check.

RaceName: Start Your Racing TV Free Trial Apprentice Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Exposed after eight starts but scores good marks for her consistency; back in a maiden after finishing fourth in two 1m handicaps this month (AW/good to firm; latest RPR 77); 7lb better off for her 0.5l defeat by Vanilla Skies at Newmarket in June; obvious chance.

RaceName: Start Your Racing TV Free Trial Apprentice Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Sold unraced out of Mick Appleby's stable for 1,000gns last September; bred to be a fair sort but likely best watched on debut.

RaceName: Start Your Racing TV Free Trial Apprentice Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Poor form in two sprint novices in the spring; step up in trip needs to give her a big lift.

RaceName: Start Your Racing TV Free Trial Apprentice Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Useful pedigree and she made an encouraging start to her career when seventh of 12, beaten under 3l, at Southwell (7f) 24 days ago; open to improvement and could have a big role to play.

Classy 6f performer who has been placed in Group 1s at that trip and she won a Group 3 at York (6f, good to firm) this month, for which she carries a 3lb penalty today; untested at 7f but she frequently finishes her races strongly, as was the case when fourth in the 2024 Group 1 Prix Maurice de Gheest at Deauville over 6.5f; leading contender if staying the trip.

5yo who was a big improver at the start of this season, winning a handicap at Newmarket (7f, good) then the Group 3 Chartwell Stakes at Lingfield (7f, good to firm); however, it appears as though she may have gone off the boil on her last two outings; carries a 3lb penalty this afternoon.
Four handicap wins at Southwell (7f/6f, AW) early this year; however, unplaced in Listed races on turf on her three outings this summer and she's up against it today.
She's gone close in Listed races at Chester (7f, good) on her last two starts, beaten just a neck last time when having to challenge wide; she might not be far away.

C&D handicap winner who was third to Royal Velvet in a Group 3 at Lingfield (7f, good to firm) in May; however, this exposed 6yo faces a tougher assignment in today's line-up and was ninth of 13 in this race 12 months ago; blew the start at Newmarket last time; hood/tongue-tie are applied.

Went very close in big-field Listed race at Deauville (7.5f, AW) last December and she may have needed the run when sixth of seven at Longchamp in April on her return (7f, good to soft; Listed); however, a clear career-best is necessary if she's to make a serious impact this afternoon.

She's thrived since joining this yard and made it 4-7 for the stable when making all in a Listed race at Pontefract (1m, good) three weeks ago; today's company demands further improvement but she might still have more to offer and could make another bold bid.

Won the Group 3 Summer Stakes at York (6f, good) last July and she's run well in defeat on both starts this season, finishing third to Flora Of Bermuda at Newmarket (6f, good to firm; Listed) before 3l ninth of 18 in the Group 1 Jubilee Stakes at Royal Ascot (6f, good to firm); stays well over 6f and this new trip is worth a go; major player if stamina isn't an issue.

Ran well in fourth behind Zanthos in the Group 2 Rockfel Stakes at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) last September on her final 2yo start; however, well beaten on both outings this season and needs to get back on track.
Won 2yo novice races last July on her first two starts and has run well in defeat in some Group and Listed races since, but she hasn't shown enough to suggest she'll be a serious contender in this.

Placed in two Group 3 races (6f/7f, soft/good to soft) and ran well for a long way when eighth of 15 in the French 1,000 Guineas at Longchamp (1m, heavy) in May; drops back in grade today and the return to 7f could also help, but others have stronger claims; unproven on good/good to firm.

Best 2yo performance came when runner-up in the Group 3 Dick Poole Stakes over 6f at Salisbury last September; flopped in the Group 1 Cheveley Park at Newmarket a fortnight later and absent since; her form needs to go to a new level on this comeback outing.

Won on debut here (6f, good) last August and beaten on next two starts (6f; including Group 3) before convincing handicap win at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) this month; this is a much tougher test of her credentials but she impressed last time and her dam was a Group 3 winner; trainer saddled two 3yos to dead-heat for first in this race 12 months ago; one to consider.

Down the field in Group 1s on her two starts this season, specifically the French 1,000 Guineas and the Commonwealth Cup at Royal Ascot; however, today's drop back in grade and first-time tongue-tie could prompt an upturn in fortunes, and she made virtually all to win the Group 2 Rockfel Stakes at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) last September; can have a big say if back on song.

RaceName: Stephen And Alan Mulley Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Off the mark on turf when beating five rivals at Doncaster (1m4f, good to soft) last month but he was beaten 8l when fifth of ten off this mark at York (1m4f, good to firm) 19 days ago; now drops back in trip.

RaceName: Stephen And Alan Mulley Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Both wins have been over 1m but she did go close over this C&D last September (good to soft); ran well at Pontefract (1m, good) two starts ago but below her best at Thirsk (good to firm) two weeks ago; steps back up in trip.

RaceName: Stephen And Alan Mulley Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: All three wins from 36 starts have been on the AW at Newcastle (6f/1m); solid effort when third at Wetherby (1m, good to firm) last month but he needs to bounce back from a lesser effort at Pontefract (1m) three weeks ago; has stamina to prove for this longer trip.

RaceName: Stephen And Alan Mulley Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Nine-race maiden; ran an encouraging race on her stable debut at Thirsk (1m4f, good) last June but returned from a year off with a heavy defeat at Hamilton (first-time tongue-tie) 55 days ago; drops back in trip and others have stronger claims.

RaceName: Stephen And Alan Mulley Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Four-time AW winner (1m/1m2f) but he's struggled since returning for this stable in January (refused to race on one occasion), albeit he did have a wide trip last time; has dropped to a career-low mark but has a bit to prove.

RaceName: Stephen And Alan Mulley Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Built on his debut when second of 11 in a novice at Newcastle (7f, AW) last month and ran to a similar level when third of six at Carlisle (1m, good to firm) 20 days ago; now makes his handicap debut but his pedigree doesn't suggest he's crying out for this longer trip.

RaceName: Stephen And Alan Mulley Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Made a winning reappearance in a 7f novice here in April (first start since being gelded) and bounced back from a couple of lesser efforts when a respectable third of six at Ripon (1m2f, good) last time; down in grade and has claims.

RaceName: Stephen And Alan Mulley Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Dual winner over 1m2f at Newcastle in 2024 but winless since; close-up fourth there at a big price in March but has struggled in three starts since, all at Newcastle; returns to turf with a bit to prove.

RaceName: Stephen And Alan Mulley Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Ended a two-year losing run when winning a Class 6 at Beverley (1m2f, good to firm) two weeks ago; steps back up in grade off this 2lb higher mark, but he has to be considered.

Speedy gelding who defied top weight in the Lily Agnes at Chester (5f, good) when last seen, taking record to 3-3; runner-up has franked that form since; sidestepped Royal Ascot and comes here fresh; respected with this scenario likely to suit and further progress possible.
Steadily progressive until form dipped in last two outings, only midfield with tongue-tie fitted in the Super Sprint latest; chance depends on how well he responds to the addition of blinkers.

Redcar maiden winner who changed ownership for £100,000 prior to belying his 150-1 odds with second-place finish in the Norfolk at Royal Ascot (5f, good to firm) last time; this thrice-raced colt is one of the main contenders, provided the latest effort is backed up.
Looked promising in winning well at Bath (5f, good to firm); soundly beaten in the Norfolk since but perhaps that assignment was too much too soon; may still have progress in him.
Unexposed but the form of his neck success at Hamilton (5f, good) last time is well below Group standard; indeed he's bottom of this pack on the figures.

550,000gns breeze-up buy who comfortably beat two rivals to win at Ayr (5f, good to firm) and was hampered en route to fading over 6f in the Coventry at Royal Ascot (eased once held; better than the bare result); retains potential and remains of interest back down in distance.
Won at Hamilton (5f) then ran well in the Windsor Castle at Royal Ascot (6f) but probably showed no further progress at Newbury last time; this assignment demands a bigger figure.
Record is 2-9, the wins in C&D seller in June and Windsor nursery last time; proving consistent but looks out of his depth upped sharply in class.

Irish challenger; has displayed major improvement since dropped back to 5f, winning a maiden then going close in Listed event, both at Naas on good ground; may have more to offer over this trip; not ruled out.

No match for impressive winner in her second start but has shown useful 5f form since, belying her 100-1 odds with good fifth in the Queen Mary then bagging Listed honours at Deauville; ties in closely with Pershaada on the Royal Ascot effort; major contender.

Beaten favourite in two AW attempts; has shown marked improvement since switched to turf, winning a C&D novice contest (good) then running well in the Queen Mary at Royal Ascot (5f, good to firm) where she was one place in front of Crownbreaker; strong claims.

RaceName: Marske Fabrications & Engineering Straight Mile Apprentice Fillies' Handicap (Straight Mile Qual)
Spotlight: Quickened up well off a steady pace to win a Chelmsford novice (1m, AW) in October and ran well when runner-up on her handicap debut at Kempton next time; has had wind surgery since and now has a tongue-tie added; contender.

RaceName: Marske Fabrications & Engineering Straight Mile Apprentice Fillies' Handicap (Straight Mile Qual)
Spotlight: Three-time winner, the most recent over this C&D in May off a 3lb lower mark; ran well at Doncaster (1m, good to firm) in July but needs to bounce back from a poor run at York (1m) four days ago.

RaceName: Marske Fabrications & Engineering Straight Mile Apprentice Fillies' Handicap (Straight Mile Qual)
OwnerName: All About York And Whatton Manor Stud
Spotlight: Won a Catterick novice over 7f in April; only seventh of ten on her handicap debut at Wetherby (7f, good to firm) next time but she ran well when runner-up at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) 26 days ago; steps up in trip and she should have more to offer after just four starts.

RaceName: Marske Fabrications & Engineering Straight Mile Apprentice Fillies' Handicap (Straight Mile Qual)
Spotlight: Off the mark at the ninth attempt when winning at Carlisle (7f, good) last month and ran another good race when bumping into an improver at Beverley (8.5f, good to firm) 25 days ago; considered off the same mark.

RaceName: Marske Fabrications & Engineering Straight Mile Apprentice Fillies' Handicap (Straight Mile Qual)
Spotlight: Had been placed on her three previous starts before landing a handicap at Carlisle (7f, good to firm) 20 days ago; just 1lb higher here and she looks well worth another try over 1m; contender.

RaceName: Marske Fabrications & Engineering Straight Mile Apprentice Fillies' Handicap (Straight Mile Qual)
Spotlight: Off the mark when winning at Wetherby (1m, good to firm) last month but she disappointed having failed to settle at Nottingham (8.5f, good to firm) next time; bounced back with a good effort at Beverley (7.5f) two weeks ago and makes the shortlist.

RaceName: Marske Fabrications & Engineering Straight Mile Apprentice Fillies' Handicap (Straight Mile Qual)
Spotlight: Won over 7f here and at Musselburgh (1m, good) in June, the latter coming off a mark 5lb lower than today's; has been held in both starts since and this prominent-racer may be high enough in the weights for now.

Grand campaigner but his last two efforts, including in the Queen Anne he'd won 12 months earlier, have spoiled an otherwise excellent record at Ascot which is the place he's most associated with; below best in both Goodwood attempts, latest when fifth of seven in this race last year; opposed.

Gelded prior to this season's impressive win at Haydock (7f Listed) and respectable fifth at Royal Ascot (6f Group 1); his 1m form comprises a respectable fifth in the 2025 Queen Anne and two lesser efforts on Australian soil; still needs to prove he's a genuine miler but he arrived late to win the 7f Group 2 Lennox here yesterday and is probably in the form of his life.

Proved somewhat resurgent with second-place finish behind Qirat over 7f at York last time, the C&D of his Group 1 success last August; however, faces a stiffer assignment back up in trip/class and possibly isn't crying out for this return to 1m, despite being a distance winner.

Largely progressive colt whose strike-rate of 7-10 includes wins this year at Meydan (Group 1) and Sandown (made all for a particularly good Group 2 performance under a penalty); collared only towards the finish by Ten Bob Tony and one other rival in the Queen Anne at Royal Ascot (good to firm) most recently, deserving credit having set a solid pace over that stiff 1m; flexible tactically and doesn't necessarily need to front-run; the pick of the older runners on ratings and duly commands respect.

Prevailed in York Group 3 when dropped back to 7f last month, benefiting from the first application of a tongue-tie, and rallied for fourth behind Lake Forest in 7f Group 2 Lennox here yesterday; well suited by Goodwood but he was a fluky 150-1 winner of this race last year, having been allowed too much rope in a pacemaking duty, and seems unlikely to repeat the feat.

OwnerName: Two Plus Three Two Plus Four
Spotlight: Better than ever this season, most recently a close third in Group 2 at Ascot (1m, good to firm) when bidding for a hat-trick after wins at Longchamp (Listed) and Epsom (Group 3); landed the Group 3 Thoroughbred Stakes at this meeting 12 months ago; faces a tougher task in this top grade but could go well in his current form.

Came off the good pace set by Opera Ballo when 50-1 winner of the Queen Anne at Royal Ascot (1m, good to firm) last time, completing a quickfire June double that was initiated over 7f at Epsom; still unexposed as a miler and has frame possibilities provided the latest piece of form is backed up.

OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Only scraped home from a closing Gstaad in the St James's Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot (good to firm) last time but the race didn't go fully smoothly and he also perhaps hit the front sooner than ideal over that stiff 1m; beat that rival more impressively at Newmarket on reappearance to become, on RPRs, the joint-best 2,000 Guineas winner since Frankel; still unbeaten (5-5) and, given his general trajectory, remains an exciting miler who could dominate this division for the rest of the season.

Ended last season with a couple of notable wins but broadly hasn't been in the same form this term and is currently well down the pecking order at Ballydoyle, as his rating reflects; bottom of this pack on said figures and is possibly in here to help with pacemaking duties for Gstaad.

OwnerName: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor
Spotlight: Rock-solid performer whose success in the Irish 2,000 Guineas is flanked by good efforts behind Bow Echo at Newmarket (beaten almost 3l, pair well clear) and Royal Ascot (nearly collared him); admittedly the bare result last time may not be fully reliable, given the way the race panned out and the stiff 1m; however, this smart colt is certainly reliable, having never finished out of the first two, and is again an important player in another rematch with his nemesis.

OwnerName: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith
Spotlight: Ran creditably in the Poulains on seasonal debut when bidding for a French Group 1 hat-trick; dropped away to finish last of six, having been pestered for the lead, in the St James's Palace Stakes since; that latest effort doesn't reflect his ability but he's again the stable second string behind Gstaad and remains below the standard required to win this prize.

Game colt whose record of 4-5 as a 2yo featured wins in the Vintage Stakes at this meeting and National Stakes at the Curragh; latter is one of two pieces of form that tie him in with Gstaad; respectable second in the Greenham at Newbury (kept to 7f) on reappearance but missed the 2,000 Guineas due to a setback; ready for a crack at 1m and, having raced only once this season, there's still some unfinished business about him; adds interest.

RaceName: Happy Big Birthday Rachel Blizzard Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: C&D winner; form dipped at Thirsk four weeks ago but she's the type to bounce back quickly; can get it wrong at the start but she is still more appealing than many.

RaceName: Happy Big Birthday Rachel Blizzard Apprentice Handicap
OwnerName: The Good Racing Company Ltd & Partner
Spotlight: Well backed at Thirsk (6f, good to firm) four weeks ago and she ran a fair race in fifth (behind Night Emperor who was poorly drawn); she may prefer a stiffer test at the trip but she is handicapped to go well.

RaceName: Happy Big Birthday Rachel Blizzard Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Ten-race maiden but he has shown winning potential this summer, notably when doing best of the low-drawn runners at Thirsk (6f, good to firm) on July 1; another solid run (7f) last time; shouldn't be far away.

RaceName: Happy Big Birthday Rachel Blizzard Apprentice Handicap
OwnerName: R Chapman, G J Daly & R J Parks
Spotlight: Two of her five wins have come at Redcar; well handicapped on 2025 best but she's yet to hit top gear this year; others have more pressing claims.

RaceName: Happy Big Birthday Rachel Blizzard Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Exposed 27-race maiden; runner-up in 6f classified events at Brighton on his last two starts (beaten favourite on each occasion); should run his race but others appeal more for win purposes.

RaceName: Happy Big Birthday Rachel Blizzard Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: 5f Catterick win in April; two solid placed efforts this month (5f and 6f, both good to firm); should make another bold bid.

RaceName: Happy Big Birthday Rachel Blizzard Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Ran poorly here at the end of May (7f, good to firm) but she otherwise has a good course record; ought to be well treated now but she isn't a solid option.

RaceName: Happy Big Birthday Rachel Blizzard Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Two creditable runs for new connections but he is an exposed 26-race maiden and may have to make do with some more minor money.

RaceName: Happy Big Birthday Rachel Blizzard Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Sprang an 80-1 shock at Chepstow (5f, good to firm) last July but nothing comparable since, including on last month's return to action.

The top-rated Arabian in training, having won eleven of his sixteen starts, three of them Group 1's; didn't seem to stay behind Lippo De Carrere in Qatar in February and didn't have a smooth passage at Abu Dhabi after that; was far too keen in France last time out and hopefully that run will have taken the fizz out of him; if he's back to his best, he's the one to beat. Official BHA Rating 129

OwnerName: Mr Yannick Schulz & Mr Eric Dell'Ova
Spotlight: Improving front runner who won a Group 3 contest in Morocco at the end of last year; this year has finished second in two Group 1 races in Qatar and most recently in Italy; will give it a good go from the front but likely to be vulnerable in the closing stages. Official BHA Rating 115

Given a marvellous ride by Mickael Barzalona to win the UK Arabian Derby last year; took his form to a new level though when beating Al Ghadeer (three-time winner of this race) in the Amir's Sword; not as good at Longchamp in May but the soft ground may well have been a factor; solid claims granted a strong pace to chase. Official BHA Rating 125
Won a Group 2 race as a three-year-old and won a minor race in Qatar over the winter; highly likely he's in here to be a pacemaker for his stable companion Lippo De Carrere. Official BHA Rating 105

Four-time globetrotting Group 1 winner who was supplemented for this race last week; at his best on quick ground which he didn't get at Longchamp in May when he was behind a couple of these. Better expected here despite this trip probably being a bit shorter than ideal. Official BHA Rating 127

Improving four-year-old who's won his last three starts despite idling very badly in the closing stages; clearly, he keeps a bit back for himself but there's no real knowing where his ceiling might lie; that said it will require a huge personal best to get involved in this company. Official BHA Rating 95

Won last year's French Derby and followed up with a second win in Group 1 company at Longchamp in the Autumn; hasn't been at her best in two runs this year and was well behind three of these at Longchamp in May; remains lightly raced, so it would be dangerous to rule her out. Official BHA Rating 117

OwnerName: Mr Mansoor Khalil M. Al Shahwani
Spotlight: Dual Group 1 winner who's only once been out of the frame; behind RB Kingmaker in Saudi Arabia earlier in the year but reversed that form at Longchamp in May when last seen; yard having a great season with the Arabians in Europe and she can't be ruled out. Official BHA Rating 120

Won four of her five starts in America her last one coming over this trip; looked as though the experience of Turf was needed on her French debut before taking her form to a new level winning a Group 1 race in Milan on an artificial surface narrowly beating Lino; gets weight all round and remains open to improvement, but more probably needed in a very strong renewal. Official BHA Rating 112

RaceName: Go Racing In Yorkshire Future Stars Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Both wins have been over 8.5f at Beverley, the most recent in April off 1lb lower than today; has been running respectably recently and drops back down in grade with solid claims.

RaceName: Go Racing In Yorkshire Future Stars Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Won here over 1m2f in May (good to firm) and followed up in a competitive handicap at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) next time; left the impression he's still in form when fifth there 11 days ago and has to be respected back at this track (2-3 here).

RaceName: Go Racing In Yorkshire Future Stars Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Off the mark when making all at Ripon (1m, good) in May and followed up at Beverley (8.5f, good to firm) next time; faded into eighth of 11 at Doncaster (1m, good to firm) 11 days ago but may get an easier time of things in front this time.

RaceName: Go Racing In Yorkshire Future Stars Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Two wins at Ripon over 1m last year (good/good to firm); respectable fourth of nine at Thirsk (1m, good to firm) in May but he's yet to build on that in four starts since; others look stronger.

RaceName: Go Racing In Yorkshire Future Stars Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: Ended a two-year losing run when winning here over 1m1f on good to firm ten days ago, beating seven rivals; still well treated on his old form under a 4lb penalty and commands respect.

RaceName: Go Racing In Yorkshire Future Stars Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: 19-race maiden; beaten 1l when second of eight at Beverley (8.5f, good) last month but she's been well beaten in two starts since, including when failing to beat a rival home there two weeks ago.

RaceName: Go Racing In Yorkshire Future Stars Apprentice Handicap
Spotlight: 3-22 on the AW (wins have been at Newcastle over 7f) compared to 1-27 on turf; has been shaping as if she's in form in recent starts and once again has each-way claims.

OwnerName: J P Morris, Mrs V A Tunnicliffe Et Al
Spotlight: Bounced back to form to win at Newmarket (6f, good) in May but two lesser runs have followed on the July Course there since.

Reappeared with a win at Catterick (6f, good) in April and then made all at Epsom (6f, good) this month; faded late on to finish sixth of seven at Hamilton since but he can be made to look well treated on the Epsom form (beat Amazing Journey) and his yard is no stranger to sprint handicap success at this meeting.

Responded well to first-time cheekpieces (retained since) when successful over 7f at Kempton in December; no more than a respectable fourth back there (7f again) two months later and off since (has been gelded); Clive Cox is among the winners but others arrive with more pressing claims.

OwnerName: SBK Racing & B & J Parr Racing Ltd
Spotlight: Made it three wins in his last five starts when seeing off five rivals at Nottingham (5f, good to firm) four weeks ago; at the top of his game but this asks a different question of one who has gained all six career successes in single-figure fields.

Enhanced a good Windsor record when seeing off next-time-out winner Amazonian Dream and ten others over 6f on good to firm 16 days ago; a 5lb rise looks manageable, particularly as she went close off 4lb higher at this meeting last year; on the shortlist.

Took advantage of a lowly mark at Southwell in December and he has flourished since, adding two more AW wins over the winter and going in again at Salisbury (6f, soft) last month; runner-up on all three outings since and likely to give it another good shot.

Sprung a 66-1 shock on her seasonal return at Hamilton (6f, good) in May but sixth is the best she's managed in three outings since; back on the mark she defied at Hamilton but others are more persuasive.
Held on grimly for a first success since his 2yo days (missed 2025) at Thirsk (6f, good) six weeks ago; only 2lb higher but that form has taken a few knocks since.

Ended his 2yo campaign with nursery wins over 6f/7f; unplaced first two runs in 2026 but back to his best in first-time cheekpieces (now replaced by the blinkers he wore on penultimate start) when second of seven at Leicester (7f, good to firm) 25 days ago.
Showed career-best form when winning at Lingfield (6f, soft) under Myla Coppins last month but has failed to reproduce it twice since.

The handicapper has been in command since his runaway win at Leicester (6f, good) in April; respectable sixth of 19 at York (6f, good to firm) 18 days ago but suspicion he'll prove vulnerable for win purposes again.
Lacks recent match practice and gained his sole win off 9lb lower but on the plus side his yard is enjoying a fine summer; worth a second look in the betting.
Ran well for second at Musselburgh (5f, good) last month; respectable fourth of 14 at York (6f, good) since but she's yet to win from a mark in the 80s.
Made all off today's mark on seasonal debut at Bath (5.7f, firm) in April; one of best runs since when 2l second of eight at Newbury (6f, good to firm) last week.

Can miss the break and is usually ridden from off the pace; back-to-back wins over the extended 5f at Brighton this summer, the latter by a wide margin under Jude Fernandes this month; below-form third turned out under a penalty at Salisbury (6f, good to firm) four days later and another 4lb higher now.

OwnerName: A Smith, J Henwood & Star Amusements
Spotlight: Off the mark at the sixth attempt at Wolverhampton (6f, AW) in February and returned to form with a gutsy handicap win at Windsor (6f, good to firm) last month; bettered that form when fourth of 11 in 7f 3yo handicap at the Newmarket July meeting and the form-figures of the four who have run out of that race since are 1113; considered under Buick.

OwnerName: Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum
Spotlight: Four 7f handicap wins on good/good to firm since May; travelled well in lead for long way when third of six off this mark at Newbury (7f, good to firm) 11 days ago; three of her wins were gained at sharp Cattrerick and she could be speedy enough to cope with a drop back to 6f.
Placed six times (7f-1m2f) before making it 12th time lucky in 7f Ascot handicap (good to firm) last Friday; has a 5lb penalty and a new trip to contend with now.

Won three times at two, including at Nottingham (6f, good to soft) off 3lb higher in October; he's performed below that level in his three outings this year but latest fifth over 5f here was a bit better and he should be suited by the return to 6f; no shock were he to bounce back to form with a bang.

Running well in defeat in 7f/1m handicaps for Brian Ellison this year; changed hands for 34,000gns this month; shrewd new yard quick to drop him back in trip (peak RPRs last year achieved over 6f); worth a second look in the betting.

500,000euros breeze-up purchase last year; left sole 2yo run behind when second over 7f at Doncaster (good to firm) on reappearance; faded over 7f on soft ground when only fifth at Carlisle since and the drop back to 6f could suit on handicap debut; unexposed contender for leading owners who target this meeting.
Wide-margin winner of 6f AW novice as 2yo but best handicap form has come at 7f and he's finished nearer last than first over 6f on his last two starts; first-time blinkers need to help.

Started 2026 with 6f AW wins at Newcastle (novice) and Southwell (handicap); best run on turf since when fourth of 11 to the reopposing Calling A Star at Windsor (6f, good to firm) six weeks ago; subsequently gelded and also fitted with a first-time tongue-tie.

All wins for former yard came over 6f; didn't run badly on stable debut at Yarmouth but well beaten at Doncaster since (both 7f); first-time blinkers go on (regularly wore cheekpieces/visor for previous stable).

Has drawn a blank since his 6f nursery debut success at Newbury last year but he did go close in 20-runner York handicap (7f, good) in May; bit below that level in two 7f outings last month but new connections went to 55,000gns to acquire him recently and Billy Loughnane has been booked.
6f winner in Ireland last term but holds weak claims on his three efforts for new stable.

All races at 6f, taking a step forward for the switch to turf when well on top from two subsequent winners in 6f Windsor maiden (good to firm) in May; a bit disappointing on last Thursday's Doncaster handicap debut but possible he needed it after ten weeks off; remains unexposed.

Half-brother to smart staying chaser Lombron; ran okay in a point-to-point and encouraging hurdles debut in 3m Punchestown maiden last month, staying on into third after being short of room going to the last (good-to-yielding); more likely needed but respected.

Flemensfirth gelding cost 70,000euros as a 3yo; brother to 2m7f chase winner Flemen's Tipple; dam 2m-2m3f hurdle/chase winner, sister to French 2m2f Listed hurdle winner Mister Snowball; disputing lead when unseated five out on point-to-point debut at Necarne in May; has since joined Gordon Elliott and market likely good guide on hurdles debut.

Placed in five of six starts over hurdles, last three for current yard, notably staying on second in valuable 2m4f auction hurdle final at Punchestown festival, most recently quicker ground and sharp track at Ballinrobe may not have been ideal when third in 2m6f maiden in late May (good); back from a break with cheekpieces tried; strong place claims again.

Mahler 5yo is first foal of a bumper winner, a sister to winners Themanintheboots (2m4f/3m hurdle) and The Brass Man (bumper); never sighted in Fairyhouse bumper last year and place claims when fell at the last in Castletown-Geoghegan point-to-point in October: probably best watched on hurdles debut.

42,000euros yearling; brother to a useful French 2m-3m hurdle/chase winner, half-brother to five winners; tongue-tied, never sighted on Punchestown maiden debut in November; may need more time but worth a market check.

Point winner has run some solid races in defeat in maiden hurdles behind decent sorts, most recently making most when second over 2m5f at Roscommon early this month (good); should run his race but more needed to play a leading role.
Court Cave gelding; runner-up twice in point-to-points in season just ended, soundly beaten both times; bought for E26,000 since; stable/rules debut.

Won Grade 2 bumper at the DRF in 2024; sidelined until April, pick of two runs in maiden hurdles when hampered early on and weakened late over extended 2m6f in finishing fourth (good); didn't seem to stay 3m at Cork on latest, drops in trip here with headgear combination tried; definite player.

Point winner in April ran a cracker on hurdles debut when third in a 3m Cork maiden following month; two runs since over shorter trips not as good, 15l off Frankie's Freebie over 2m5f at Roscommon on latest; bit to find.
Sent off at odds-on for a maiden point at Ballindenisk last November, never threatened when moderate fourth for Andy Slattery; reappears for new yard on hurdles debut.

Plenty of promise in 2024, in bumpers and maiden hurdles; not near that level of form until recent return from a break in 2m2f Cork maiden in first-time tongue-tie, every chance when taking heavy fall two out; could go well if staying.
Very modest form in maidens and pulled up in all three handicaps; hard to fancy.

Group 3 winner on the Flat (1m2f, heavy; effective on good); bought for 80,000euros and gelded after winning over 1m4f in France last September; Killarney hurdles debut (2m4f) in May was okay, following month fine third in 2m6f Queen Alexandra Stakes at Ascot on good-to-firm; classy sort should be well up to winning a maiden such as this.
Placed in a point-to-point, two maiden hurdle efforts suggest he's more one for handicaps in due course, although longer trip could suit.
Maiden in point-to-points, well held in Wexford bumper, bit more encouraging in Ballinrobe maiden hurdle eight days ago but unlikely to make the improvement needed here.

Brother to yard's point/3m hurdle winner Rebel Budz; dam unraced sister to useful 2m/2m1f hurdle winner Hearts Are Trumps, out of unraced sister to Cheltenham Gold Cup winner Denman; never counted on Cork debut back in April, seems best watched on return.
Tailed off on recent hurdles debut at Cork, easily passed over.
Pulled up after never counting on hurdles debut in Limerick 4yo maiden in March; can only be watched for now.

Half-sister to Cheltenham Gold Cup winner Al Boum Photo has won bumpers at Sligo last summer and most recently at Punchestown last month, comfortably landing odds in 2m1f mares' contest (good-to-yielding); also finished second to a smart type at last year's Galway festival; potentially smart recruit to hurdles, major player.

Two Flat wins include 1m4f maiden at this meeting in 2024 (also second in 2m handicap here last year); 0-6 hurdling however, has had a break since midfield in 2m3f Leopardstown mares handicap in early March; has to be respected from a yard doing no wrong but has to improve on what we've seen so far.

RaceName: Tote.ie Money-Back 2nd Every Race Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Won over fences here in October (2m6f) and followed up in a handicap hurdle at Limerick (3m); encouraging return from a break when going close at Killarney 12 days ago and he's in the mix.

RaceName: Tote.ie Money-Back 2nd Every Race Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: 0-5 over hurdles and best form has been over fences, winning in March and twice runner-up since then; poor last time (second run in this headgear combination) but he's an assured stayer at this trip on his return to hurdles.

RaceName: Tote.ie Money-Back 2nd Every Race Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Should give his running on the back of respectable shows in 3m/2m6f handicaps but he's stuck on a tough enough mark.

RaceName: Tote.ie Money-Back 2nd Every Race Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Dual hurdles winner at about this trip and won over fences this May; went close off 4lb lower in a Fairyhouse handicap hurdle in January the last time he was ridden by Anna McGuinness.

RaceName: Tote.ie Money-Back 2nd Every Race Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Sole Flat success came in a 1m4f handicap at this meeting three years ago and later that year he won a maiden hurdle; no joy since though and was struggling when last seen over hurdles.

RaceName: Tote.ie Money-Back 2nd Every Race Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Won a 2m2f handicap at Listowel in September when 4lb lower; below that level since and this is no easy race in which to bounce back.

RaceName: Tote.ie Money-Back 2nd Every Race Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Modest strike-rate and was in no form when last seen during the winter; hard to recommend.

RaceName: Tote.ie Money-Back 2nd Every Race Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Case can be made off this mark on best of his form and has run quite well in a pair of 2m3f handicaps for current yard; possibilities back up to a trip that he does stay.

RaceName: Tote.ie Money-Back 2nd Every Race Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Dual hurdle winner who got off the mark as a chaser five days ago in a 2m4f handicap at Kilbeggan; that was a narrow verdict and he's 5lb higher this afternoon, but he's clearly in good nick.

RaceName: Tote.ie Money-Back 2nd Every Race Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Modest on the Flat; well beaten on handicap debut over hurdles in May but had some useful juvenile form and wouldn't be without hope should this new headgear combination trigger a return to that level.

RaceName: Tote.ie Money-Back 2nd Every Race Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Sligo maiden hurdle winner but yet to offer too much in handicaps and has stamina to prove over this far; first-time cheekpieces.

RaceName: Tote.ie Money-Back 2nd Every Race Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: 0-8 on the Flat; an improving hurdler having won at Kilbeggan 19 days ago (2m2f, good) and brings potential into handicaps; unraced over this far.

RaceName: Tote.ie Money-Back 2nd Every Race Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Hurdle/chase winner; didn't look an easy ride when beaten about 10l off this mark at Kilbeggan five days ago.

RaceName: Tote.ie Money-Back 2nd Every Race Handicap Hurdle
OwnerName: John J Cullen & Michael C Barrett
Spotlight: All three hurdle wins have come at Sligo where he went close 17 days ago (3m1f, good); has something to prove away from that venue but he's not without hope.

RaceName: Tote.ie Money-Back 2nd Every Race Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Won a novice handicap here in October but struggled since and latest third was quite remote and in a claimer.

RaceName: Tote.ie Money-Back 2nd Every Race Handicap Hurdle
OwnerName: Mickey D's Bus Tangara Five Syndicate
Spotlight: Lightly raced for Henry De Bromhead but she signed off for that yard with a maiden win (2m3f, soft; sold on for £10,000); could have more to offer for new yard but lacks a recent run and may prefer softer ground.

RaceName: Tote.ie Money-Back 2nd Every Race Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Dual point winner who was third in a hunter chase last time; doesn't have the obvious profile for this race but she showed useful form in 2023 when runner-up in a Leopardstown maiden and she needs checking in the betting on debut for Emmet Mullins.

RaceName: Tote.ie Money-Back 2nd Every Race Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Positively ridden when fourth in a 2m3f maiden at Kilbeggan latest; lightly raced 6yo contesting only his second handicap and has new headgear; not entirely dismissed.

RaceName: Tote.ie Money-Back 2nd Every Race Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Point and maiden hurdle winner; tailed off over hurdles (first-time blinkers) before pulled up in a handicap chase (first-time cheekpieces); others safer.

RaceName: Tote.ie Money-Back 2nd Every Race Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Placed in French bumpers and again in one of his four runs for Nicky Henderson whom he left for £25,000; has low mileage and Jack Kennedy is booked; could be interesting.

Very capable performer but he can race freely and has been in and out in four starts for this yard; beat Zarathos to take 7f handicap at Epsom (good to soft; Crimson Spirit fourth) on Oaks day and, following a lesser effort at Royal Ascot, he was back in respectable form when fifth in the Bunbury Cup (good to firm; first-time hood) this month; James Doyle sticks with him but no hood today and has the widest stall.

Finished a fairly close fourth in this last year (good) when the pick of James Doyle from three Wathnan runners; had been gelded before taking a 7f handicap at Kempton (AW) on his reappearance in the spring but it's been downhill in two subsequent starts; hopes pinned on his second visit to Goodwood sparking a revival.

Unraced at two but he scored twice around this trip on turf as a 3yo; built on his Chester comeback in May with neck second of 14 in fairly valuable Newcastle handicap (7f, AW) one month ago; that wasn't far off his best and he may still be capable of better; respected.

OwnerName: Emma Banks, David Manasseh & Austin Whelan
Spotlight: A handicapping case can be made on last year's Irish form but he's been slow to get going for this yard and a wide stall is unlikely to help him stage a revival.

Three-time 7f turf winner who finished eighth of 16 in the 3yo handicap over C&D at this meeting last year for James Owen; had been gelded before finishing down the field in first two starts for this yard but was close to career-best form when second of 17 at York (7f, good to firm) 19 days ago; that was a bunch finish but 1lb nudge still looks reasonable; considered despite tricky stall.

It was a convincing win when she beat 13 others to land a valuable handicap from 6lb lower over C&D (good) last May; this season started well with two placed efforts at Newmarket (7f, good to firm/good) in May but she disappointed when beaten 15l to finish last of 10 on the July course 25 days ago; that can probably be forgiven as she raced in a group that was never competitive.

He progressed well over this trip last term and, following a slow start to this season, he was back in the groove in first-time blinkers when scoring at Chester (7f, good to firm) earlier in the month; finished close sixth at York (Pellitory second) under a penalty one week later and he's not readily dismissed.
Tends to reserve his best for Meydan and he hasn't landed a telling blow in valuable handicaps at Royal Ascot and Newmarket on his last two starts; well drawn and he drops in grade, though.

Just one novice stakes win for Hugo Palmer but recorded plenty of good efforts, including when he split two subsequent Group winners in a 1m conditions race here (good) last May; didn't run badly in three of four starts in Meydan for this yard earlier in the year, but his British return from a 111-day break was underwhelming last month; might have needed that and he's not badly treated.

In good form since returning to turf in the spring, getting the better of Silver Ghost to score at Newmarket (good) in May before solid third on the July course (again 7f, good to firm) the following month; just caught out by a drop to 6f when fourth at Ascot 19 days ago but that form is working out well; player back at 7f with William Buick taking over.

Three wins last year and he won 14-runner handicap over C&D (good) in May; solid fourth to Colombier at Epsom next time and it was a narrow career best when second of 11 at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) 18 days ago; will probably need another pb but that's not out of the question and Ryan Moore rides; considered.

Norwegian raider who has won from 5.5f to 1m1f in his homeland, including three wins on turf (6f, good); comes here in good nick having been beaten just a neck over this trip at Ovrevoll (good) three weeks ago but stall 17 isn't overly helpful; sports a hood.

His two runner-up efforts in a Qatar conditions turf event and Lingfield Listed race (also 7f, AW) last spring would give him serious claims off this mark; didn't beat a rival in three subsequent handicaps but he had been gelded when showing more at Newcastle last time; that came after a 127-day break and he could go well at potentially big odds.

Bit of a legend down the years and his six wins here include two at Glorious Goodwood, namely a heavy-ground edition of this in 2023 and when bagging valuable Golden Mile (soft) last term; now 6lb lower but there's a reason for that and he could do with a downpour, which isn't forecast; has a good stall and Oisin Murphy retakes the reins, however, while that course record means he can never be overlooked.

OwnerName: J Sarkar, D Sarkar, O Sarkar & D Sarkar
Spotlight: He has taken it up a notch this season, winning at Windsor (1m, good to firm; made most) in May and beating 21 others under a penalty at York (7f, good) eight days later; fine second to Colombier at Epsom next time and his latest fifth in valuable Curragh handicap (1m) was respectable; has to be of interest again.

Beaten on his last 16 starts going back to May 2024 and he didn't deliver on a hint he was on the way back at Chester in May when beaten 7l at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) 25 days ago; just 1lb above his last winning mark, however, and first-time blinkers might help him put his best foot forward.

Scored at York for Andrew Balding on his last run in this grade; quite highly tried in seven starts for this yard but he was far from disgraced when third of five in a Swedish Listed event (7f, good) one month ago; tongue-tie added and he has one of the widest stalls to contend with, however.

A couple of close calls led to a frustrating campaign last year but it was a good effort when a running-on fourth to Crimson Spirit over C&D (good) in May; not seen since but he's dipped below his last winning mark and this may have been the plan; big run might be on the cards.

Eight-time winner who has been kept busy since joining this yard and he rattled off a four-timer on AW (7f/1m) earlier in the year; has been knocking on the door of late, including when close third of 17 at York (7f, good to firm; Pellitory second; Morte Point sixth) 19 days ago; firmly in the mix once again.

He was making hay in AW claimers earlier in the year, winning three of his last four races (6f-1m) for Denis Hogan and he carried on the good work when taking a Kempton handicap (1m, AW) at 25-1 on his stable debut four weeks ago; up 4lb but he used to act on turf and can't be discounted from a good stall.

Bang-in-form 4yo who comes here after emphatic wins under Seamus Cronin at Ascot and Pontefract (both 1m, good to firm) this month; competes off career-high mark but must be considered in current mood.

Probably better known for his AW exploits nowadays but he led close home to cause 28-1 surprise on recent stable debut at Ripon (1m, good), his ninth career success; nudged up only 1lb for that and is a rare runner here for his Middleham-based trainer; respected.

Four good runs this season, the latest a close second at Epsom (8.5f, good to firm; first-time cheekpieces) three weeks ago; went  up 3lb for that but the form was boosted when the winner followed up on Friday; ought to be right in the thick of things again.

Dual AW winner (7f/6f) who kept on for respectable third of six here (7f, good to firm) this month; needs to find something extra today but his pedigree and running style suggest he's well worth a go over 1m.

Bettered low-key debut when narrow winner of Chepstow maiden (7f, good to firm) in May but was last of four on recent handicap/AW debut; remains lightly raced and might be happier back on turf but others appeal more.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: This half-sister to four winners showed only minor promise on debut at Doncaster and at Newmarket four weeks later; more is needed back in trip.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Cost 220,000gns as a yearling and is a half-sister to dual Group 2 winner Chindit; well backed on debut at Goodwood in May (6f, good) and showed up well for a long way before her early exertions/immaturity told; good step forward highly likely.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Cost 180,000gns as a yearling; outsider of six on debut at Nottingham this month (6f, good to firm) but managed fourth to yard's other runner; showed obvious signs of greenness there and can improve.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Sixth foal; closely related to winners Marrakech Moon (7f/1m, including 2yo/France; RPR 95) and Mr Marrakech (7f AW; 93) and half-sister to two other winners at up to 1m4f; dam 5f-6.5f winner (including USA; 90); trainer has had a few 2yo winners this year, including first time out; market check advised.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Mares Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Had 50 days off before winning over fences in October and returning from 245 days away when narrowly following up in a handicap hurdle at Downpatrick (2m3f, good; 6lb lower); a likeable type who should give this a good shot.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Mares Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Lightly raced mare who was initially highly tried by Willie Mullins; hooded when making the most of a huge drop in class at Tramore (2m4f maiden) but ran miserably when odds-on at Kilbeggan; not easy to assess ahead of this handicap debut.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Mares Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Competitive form in 2024 and missed the following year; won two soft-ground handicaps for new yard earlier this year but she's fine on good and latest run at Bellewstown was after three months off; now visored.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Mares Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Finished well to finish second in this 12 months ago when only 1lb lower; could be glad to see the back of fences (0-3) and one to consider.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Mares Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Dual bumper winner who beat 15 rivals in a Killarney maiden in May (2m6f); quick enough for this sharper test and dangerously unexposed now handicapping.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Mares Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: It wasn't a strong maiden she won at Bellewstown (2m4f, good) but merits respect all the same as a handicap debutante from a top yard.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Mares Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Had lost her way but firmly back on track now and won comfortably at Tramore; back up 6lb in a deeper race but considered.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Mares Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Ex-French; Fakenham winner on yard debut and even better since then, finishing third in a Listed hurdle before a near miss at Cartmel (2m1f, good; handicap debut); interesting runner for a British yard going great runs; first-time cheekpieces.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Mares Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: 1-6 in points; Downpatrick maiden hurdle winner but twice pulled up since then, latterly on handicap debut in April.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Mares Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Had flashes of good form under both codes for previous yard, whom she left after finishing tailed off in this 12 months ago (went off too fast); lurks on a reasonable mark on just her second run for Joseph O'Brien; finished last in the first (1m maiden) but that was after a long break so could strip fitter now.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Mares Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Just three runs over hurdles and won a Killarney maiden by 10l last August; made all in a 1m1f maiden last month when tried in first-time cheekpieces; could have a part to play.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Mares Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Point/maiden hurdle winner who ran surprisingly well on unfavourable terms at Clonmel last time (2m3f); unwise to take that form at face value.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Mares Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Fit off the Flat and she was quite a convincing winner of this 12 months ago off 7lb lower; raced only once over hurdles in the meantime.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Mares Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Useful form for previous yards; still early days with Charles Byrnes and perhaps went off too fast in maiden company at Kilbeggan (2m2f, good; favourite); often leads and dominating a field of this size won't be easy.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Mares Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Bellewstown maiden hurdle winner in April and following handicap run at Wexford looked too bad to be true; still lightly raced.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Mares Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Only fifth when favourite last time but perhaps the ground was too soft having previously finished second in 2m1f/2m4f handicaps on quicker surfaces; after seven races there's scope for further improvement.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Mares Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Stable won this in 2022 and 2023; this mare is 0-9 over hurdles but has finished runner-up seven times, including her sole handicap start two outings ago; looks handicapped about right but has each-way claims.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Mares Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Progressing and might have won on her handicap debut at Cork but for some interference (2m4f, good); this drop in distance isn't an obvious positive but one to bear in mind.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Mares Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Comfortably saw off Sea Of Doubt at Downpatrick two weeks ago (2m2f, good) but she went up 8lb for that and doesn't always follow one good run with another.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Mares Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Well beaten in this 12 months ago; looks in better form now, winning at Downpatrick in May and solid since then (including over fences two runs ago); no match for Small Bucks last time but she's 7lb better off with that rival; unseated rider at first fence 5.45 on Tuesday.

Ended 2025 with three consecutive 6f AW wins and was successful twice on turf in the spring (5.7f/6f); does not have much margin for error off current mark, though, and this 63rd career start is his first over 5f.

Showed career-best form when winning readily at Musselburgh (5f, soft) in April and is also effective on fast ground but his subsequent efforts this spring were underwhelming; non-runner at Goodwood yesterday.

Low-mileage 3yo who began this season with two perfectly respectable runs (one over C&D) and did well to take modest third after losing ground at the start at Redcar (5f, good) last month; edging down the weights; big player if he breaks on terms.
Absent since disappointing seasonal/handicap debut over C&D in April and has the wing draw today but he was gelded during his three-month break and could still have significant potential.

OwnerName: B D Haynes, G L Moore, Alan Jamieson
Spotlight: Came from the rear to score at Newbury last month and was placed off today's mark at Epsom (also 6f, good to firm) three weeks ago; can probably cope with this drop back to a stiff 5f but he'll need some luck from stall 1 and his tendency to start slowly is also a worry.

Won Leicester maiden (5f, good to firm) last summer; may not have been suited by good to soft ground when disappointing on final 2yo start but has fitness to prove after ten-month break; has been gelded.

RaceName: Every Race Live On Racing TV Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Confirmed promise of debut second on AW in April (form worked out well) when beating the odds-on favourite at Chepstow 13 days ago (also 5f; good to firm); could well make a winning start in nurseries.

RaceName: Every Race Live On Racing TV Nursery Handicap
OwnerName: Fairies At The Bottom Of The Garden Ltd
Spotlight: Improver in RPR terms and showed a lot of speed at Windsor last time with only the 2-9 favourite and a runner who went on to finish second to Amber Ocean going by in the final furlong; can step forward again in this his first nursery.

RaceName: Every Race Live On Racing TV Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Ran to RPR of 63 or 64 each start, most recently on nursery debut at Yarmouth three weeks ago; could have done without a 2lb rise for being beaten over a length; yard ended quiet spell with 16-1 winner yesterday.

RaceName: Every Race Live On Racing TV Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Claimed out of Karl Burke's yard for 20,000gns in May; the step up to 6f looked in her favour when starting out for new connections at Ripon six weeks ago but she bombed out; the ridges at that track aren't for everyone and you can probably put a line through that effort; redemption might be tricky back over 5f here; nursery debut.

RaceName: Every Race Live On Racing TV Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Recorded RPR of 59 when third on debut at Thirsk in May (5f, good) and ran to same figure/filled same position at Hamilton the following month (5f, good to firm; sent off evens); failed to quicken once in the clear last time and is opposable kept to the minimum trip for nursery debut.

RaceName: Every Race Live On Racing TV Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Improved as he's dropped back in trip from 7f and showed plenty of zip when third of 11 at Bath four weeks ago (5.7f, firm); looks well worth a go over the bare 5f; considered on nursery debut.

Rated this high for a reason and was never headed when beating Three Card Brag in a Grade 3 at Killarney when last seen in May; however, he'll do well to repeat those tactics in this race and he was well beaten last year (held up).

For one who stays much further he ran surprisingly well when splitting Senecia and Jess Evans in a 2m4f Grade 3 at Killarney last time, which was his first run over that sort of trip since 2023; he knows what these big-field handicaps are all about and could run well at lengthy odds with a 7lb claimer easing his burden.

Grade 1-placed over hurdles and already a better chaser, making it 2-4 in this discipline when a well-backed 3l winner of a strong 2m4f novice handicap at Punchestown in May (2m4f, yielding); took an 8lb hit for that but the ceiling of his ability is not yet established and he should stay this far; Townend's pick of the Mullins runners.

Lacks course form over fences; smart novice who ran creditably in two strong handicaps (3m2f/2m5f) last season before finishing tailed off in the Grand National at Aintree where not a lot went right (twice badly hampered; 20-1); enters the reckoning.

Course winner; off for 110 days but proven when fresh; last season ended on a high with his second to a handicap snip in the Plate at Cheltenham in March (2m4f) and then going one better when reversing those placings in the Topham at Aintree (2m5f); straightforward and a good jumper who should be well suited by the demands of this race; player.

Course winner; this meeting owes him one having twice finished runner-up in the Galway Hurdle (and fourth) and second in this last year behind Western Fold; returns off a 2lb lower mark despite beating notable opposition at Listowel on final run; solid chance.

Beat Will The Wise on his chase debut here last October and followed up in a Grade 3; appeared stretched by nearly 3m in the Mayo National before a determined victory back over 2m4f at Kilbeggan (cheekpieces returned); this intermediate trip might be just the ticket.

Some inconsistency has crept in but off a reduced mark and running in just the tongue-tie, he returned to form with a second of 14 behind Solitary Man in the Midlands National at Kilbeggan (3m1f, good); whether he'll repeat that remains to be seen and he probably appreciates further than 2m6f these days.

Absent for 141 days but returns with his yard in great form; only had five runs over fences, winning twice and better than ever when a 10l fourth in the 2m4f Plate at the Cheltenham Festival; that form can be upgraded as he was hampered on a couple of occasions and has a useful pull in the weights with runner-up Will The Wise; yet to tackle this far under rules but he won a 3m point; tempting.

Fourth in last year's Stayers' Hurdle at Cheltenham; successful chase debut over 2m2f here last September and two good runs in defeat afterwards, including a Grade 2; after two runs over hurdles he returned to fences in a handicap at Roscommon and excuses came to light afterwards; too talented to dismiss.

Point, bumper and maiden hurdle winner; record of 2-8 over fences and signed off for previous yard on a high, winning a small-field Grade 3 before outrunning his odds behind last year's Galway Plate hero Western Fold in a 3m1f Grade 1 novice chase at Punchestown in April; intriguing runner now with Gordon Elliott, who has won this five times.

2-4 over fences, though not seen in this discipline since well held in a Grade 3 at this fixture two years ago; he returns in excellent form, in recent weeks winning on the Flat (2m) and over hurdles at Cork (3m); could have a big run in him.
A better hurdler than chaser but rated accordingly; however, he was a disappointing favourite in the Mayo National when last seen two months ago; others are more intriguing.

Progressive chaser but went up 10lb for winning a 2m4f Grade 3 in April and he came up short back in a handicap at Wexford, though still ran well and probably found the 2m3f trip sharp enough; each-way possibilities, though regular partner Darragh O'Keeffe has deserted him this time.

OwnerName: E Lynch & T C Quinn & John J McGrath
Spotlight: Smart staying hurdler/chaser who made a mistake at the wrong time when beaten about 18l in this 12 months ago when 5lb higher; failed to threaten afterwards in both disciplines, and again in a recent run on the Flat; others appeal more.

4-13 over hurdles and 1-5 as a chaser; unlikely that he gave his true running when a beaten favourite behind Nouvotic last time and his previous fourth over 2m4f at the Cheltenham Festival raises optimism; Townend has turned elsewhere, however.

One-time smart hurdler; three chase wins in the space of four runs last year included a beginners chase at this meeting and a 2m2f Grade 3 at Punchestown; hasn't kicked on at all from that sequence and he'd be a surprise winner.

Dual hurdle winner; beat Ballygunner Castle to get off the mark as a chaser at Naas and for one so inexperienced he did well to finish a 6l third behind Funiculi Funicula in a 22-runner handicap at Punchestown in May (2m4f, yielding); has low mileage for a 9yo and there could be more to come; finished second in a bumper on one previous visit to Galway.

OwnerName: Shanahan/Mrs M V Magnier/Mrs Carthy/Mrs Bartlett
Spotlight: Won a hunter chase in May and last time returned to his best when emerging from off a strong pace to beat Perceval Legallois in the 3m1f Midlands National at Kilbeggan; ideally wants further than this but a solid pace would help in that respect; back up 7lb.

The winner of two bumpers and a maiden hurdle; this is a big ask for a maiden over fences (0-4) but his seconds read well (pushed Spread Boss Ted close in one of those) and he looked in need of further than 2m4f when behind that rival and Funiculi Funicula on his handicap debut at Punchestown; could deliver the career best this race demands.

Useful three-time winner over hurdles; didn't look that progressive as a chaser until comfortably beating 20 rivals in a 3m Listed handicap at Punchestown in May; a 6lb rise could have been worse and he's now 2-3 under J J Slevin; couldn't put a line through him.

Career best form when fourth in the Paddy Power Gold Cup at Cheltenham in November (2m4f, soft); back from a break with two seconds, though was no match for the winner on either occasion (including Nouvotic); travels well but doesn't always find much for pressure.

RaceName: Chasemore Farm EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Cost 700,000euros as a yearling and is out of a French 1m 2yo Listed winner; defied market weakness when narrow winner of valuable Doncaster novice (7f, good to firm) three weeks ago and sets a useful form standard.

RaceName: Chasemore Farm EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 115,000euros yearling; fifth foal; half-brother to German Derby winner Dardanos and three other German winners (one at Listed level); dam French/German 1m2f-1m4f winner; likely to need much further than 7f to be seen to best effect.

RaceName: Chasemore Farm EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 200,000gns foal; first foal; dam 1m/1m4f winner (RPR 98), half-sister to winners Lovely Memory (1m) and Folk Melody (7f 2yo; dam of top-class 1m-1m2f performer Romantic Warrior), out of Canadian 1m2f Grade 1 winner; good market support will bring him into the equation.

RaceName: Chasemore Farm EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 320,000gns yearling; eighth foal; half-brother to four winners including Running Lion (1m/1m2f including 2yo/Group 2; RPR 116), Majestic Glory (6f/7f 2yo including Group 3; 99) and Cozone (1m2f/2m, 87); dam 1m1f/1m2f winner (92); interesting newcomer.

RaceName: Chasemore Farm EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
OwnerName: HM The King & HM The Queen
Spotlight: Third foal; half-brother to winners Crown Estate (1m; RPR 100) and Portcullis (1m; 97); dam French 1,000 Guineas winner, half-sister to 7f Listed winner Top Score; makes strong appeal on paper.

RaceName: Chasemore Farm EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
OwnerName: Oti Racing P Inglett S De Zoete &partner
Spotlight: Has two Australian Group winners among his siblings but was never better than midfield when 66-1 for recent debut at Newbury (6f, good to firm).

RaceName: Leicester Racecourse Ideal Self-Hire Wedding Venue Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Justified favouritism on debut over C&D last September (good to soft) but he raced too freely for his own good when trying to defy the same 7lb penalty as tonight at Newmarket the following month (also 7f, good); not seen since but was gelded in his time off; could be the answer.

RaceName: Leicester Racecourse Ideal Self-Hire Wedding Venue Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Uncompetitive in bumpers/over hurdles for Dylan Cunha and changed hands for 6,000gns this month; new trainer is more than capable of turning things around but 7f might be on the sharp side; rivals are all 3yos.

RaceName: Leicester Racecourse Ideal Self-Hire Wedding Venue Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Has achieved similar RPRs in all four starts but latest effort (here) was underwhelming given he'd shaped so well over that 1m2f trip at Newbury the time before; this strong traveller could get away with dropping back to 7f and is a key player.

RaceName: Leicester Racecourse Ideal Self-Hire Wedding Venue Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 160,000gns yearling; sixth foal; Starman half-brother to three winners (5f-1m1f); dam 7f AW winner (RPR 65); already gelded; this looks a good starting point and market can guide.

RaceName: Visit Tote26 On Course Today (Q.R.) Maiden
Spotlight: Tailed off in a Listowel bumper last September and in rear on Flat debut at Roscommon in May; can be ruled out.

RaceName: Visit Tote26 On Course Today (Q.R.) Maiden
Spotlight: Promise on debut in Punchestown bumper last month and again later in month (well backed) in 1m4f Roscommon Flat maiden, staying on third after not clear run; likely has more to offer.

RaceName: Visit Tote26 On Course Today (Q.R.) Maiden
Spotlight: 149-rated hurdler, gaining fifth hurdle success at Ballinrobe in May; beaten by the unconsidered Counting Coup in a Flat maiden at Down Royal before odds-on defeat over hurdles at Limerick; didn't get into valuable amateur handicap here on Monday, potentially big player in maiden company here.

RaceName: Visit Tote26 On Course Today (Q.R.) Maiden
Spotlight: Long-standing maiden in both codes; hard to fancy.

RaceName: Visit Tote26 On Course Today (Q.R.) Maiden
Spotlight: Smart Flat pedigree; looked good when justifying prohibitive odds on debut in Listowel bumper in September 2023 (good) but was unable to build on that twice afterwards on softer ground; absent since December 2023 and makes hurdles debut with ground likely to suit and clearly goes well fresh.

RaceName: Visit Tote26 On Course Today (Q.R.) Maiden
Spotlight: Ran once in a bumper and 0-4 hurdling, pick being fourth in a Roscommon maiden on good ground, last of 15 on latest in Killarney handicap; seems an unlikely one to make an impact on Flat debut.

RaceName: Visit Tote26 On Course Today (Q.R.) Maiden
Spotlight: Took well to hurdles, winning at Ballinrobe and Listowel last year before good second at Punchestown in October; fair Flat form over shorter trips than today's so stamina concerns on comeback run.

RaceName: Visit Tote26 On Course Today (Q.R.) Maiden
Spotlight: Has done well over hurdles this year, winning 2m6f Downpatrick handicap last month and good second off revised mark since at Cartmel and Downpatrick; first start on the Flat since finishing second in this race last year and could go well again.

RaceName: Visit Tote26 On Course Today (Q.R.) Maiden
Spotlight: Dual-purpose maiden for Charles O'Brien rated a meagre 54 on the Flat; hard to fancy on yard debut.

RaceName: Visit Tote26 On Course Today (Q.R.) Maiden
Spotlight: Dual bumper winner and maiden hurdle winner; fine comeback run and Flat debut when second at Killarney (1m6f, good) earlier this month and top amateur rider remains loyal.

RaceName: Visit Tote26 On Course Today (Q.R.) Maiden
Spotlight: Poor strike rate hurdling (1-25) and pick of three recent runs on the Flat when staying on late into second in 1m4f Tramore maiden (found to have in blood in both nostrils); interesting but this is a stronger maiden.

RaceName: Visit Tote26 On Course Today (Q.R.) Maiden
