Spotlight: Hurdle rating went up to a career-high 132 after winning 2m5f Killarney mares event 13 days ago, needing every yard to get up close home (good); one to consider on Flat debut.

RaceName: Visit Tote26 On Course Today (Q.R.) Maiden
Spotlight: Lightly raced son of Frankel has been gelded since finishing second to an odds-on shot in 1m2f Cork maiden in May, having run green; one-time Irish Derby entry could well have more to offer from a yard with such a fine Galway record.

RaceName: Visit Tote26 On Course Today (Q.R.) Maiden
Spotlight: Improvement on second maiden start to finish fourth over 1m5f at Ballinrobe in May, withdrawn on account of quick ground at Leopardstown since; noteworthy jockey booking and yard in fine form.

RaceName: Visit Tote26 On Course Today (Q.R.) Maiden
Spotlight: Holds quite a lofty rating, unable to justify it on last month's handicap debut at Down Royal when left with plenty to do in Ulster Derby; previous maiden runs over shorter were solid efforts; stamina now proven and should go well under more positive ride.

RaceName: Visit Tote26 On Course Today (Q.R.) Maiden
Spotlight: Placed on four of six attempts for Charlie Johnston in Britain, including all three starts on AW last winter when wearing cheekpieces; bought for 45,000gns in February and debuts for new yard with Harry Swan booked.

RaceName: Visit Tote26 On Course Today (Q.R.) Maiden
Spotlight: Decent efforts last two maiden runs at 1m2f, every chance when third at Gowran and again positively-ridden when fourth behind a smart type at the Curragh; not certain to stay this longer trip but a player if he does.

Placed in sole German start; fifth is the best he's managed in a trio of 1m maiden/novice events (good to firm-good to soft) since coming to Britain but handicaps provide him with a much more realistic chance of success and his yard is in form.
Failed to progress in his qualifying runs and his hopes are pinned on first-time blinkers sparking improvement now switching to handicaps.

Runner-up over 7f on all three 2yo starts but has failed to beat a rival in two handicaps this time round; well handicapped if recapturing her juvenile form, particularly with a useful claimer taking 5lb off, but a leap of faith is needed.

0-6; encouraging third on 1m2f Chester handicap debut and reappearance but has failed to built on it twice since; needs a drop back in trip and different headgear (first-time visor replaces cheekpieces) to help spark a revival.

Left last year's debut behind when springing an 80-1 surprise in 1m1f novice at Hamilton (good to firm) on her reappearance in May but has disappointed in two handicaps since; still early days but hard to be confident.

Best effort when keeping-on third over 7f here (good) in June, his second handicap; sold out of Richard Hannon's yard for 25,000gns this month; the way he kept on here last time suggests the return to 1m may help; leading claims with new stable among the winners.

Improved with each of his three runs on the AW, winning novice at Wolverhampton in January, but he failed to beat a rival in two turf handicaps in the spring; needs to recapture his AW form back from a break.
Well held in his three runs (1m-1m2f); pulled hard on the first two and has a hood added for handicap debut; bred to be better than a lowly opening mark of 60.
Nine-race maiden who was second on his handicap debut in April but has gone backwards since, including always behind at Epsom only 13 days ago.

Achieved one of her best RPRs when back from a break at Thirsk last April (runner-up; 6f, good) and when starting out for George Baker following a break at Kempton in November (6f; won when sporting this headgear combination for the first time); not quite so effective in two runs since but yard is now red hot; respected; withdrawn after showing reluctance to post at Salisbury recently.

Having third start for new connections when making virtually all over this trip at Wolverhampton this month; a definite player if subsequent defeat off this revised mark can be attributed to 7f rather than his first taste of ground quicker than good.

Beaten after trading at 1.23 in running at Wolverhampton in March, then recorded third win for James Owen there (6f; beat Rye by 2l); having first run on turf for the yard when weakening into sixth over C&D when last seen in April; absence of regular headgear is a concern this evening.

Placed just once in first 13 starts but has hit form of late, defeating 15 rivals at Doncaster last month (6f) and did the business over C&D (also good to firm) 25 days ago; her second in between those wins is strong form for the grade; will take all the beating off just 2lb higher than last time.

Failed to beat a rival on stable debut at Wolverhampton last month when returning from 137 days off (typically started slowly); tongue-tie returns and is a dual winner on turf (5f; one on good to firm) but hard to support.

RaceName: Tote Every Day Is A Money-Back Day Handicap
Spotlight: Debut juvenile winner a year ago (7f, Leopardstown); opened 3yo campaign in Group 3 company, notably 3.5l off subsequent US Grade 1 winner Kensingston Lane in Athasi Stakes (Curragh); never really landed a blow on handicap debut at same venue in late May (1m), cheekpieces tried.

RaceName: Tote Every Day Is A Money-Back Day Handicap
Spotlight: Had a run in a barrier trial last year; shaped promisingly when third behind the smart Sparan Nua in Naas maiden (1m) in May and following month landed similar contest, despite running green, good chance she'll improve again on handicap debut although opening mark looks high enough.

RaceName: Tote Every Day Is A Money-Back Day Handicap
Spotlight: Limerick maiden winner went up 8lb after finishing second to an older rival in Listowel conditions event; ran to similar level when fourth in rated race at Leopardstown, weakening close home; prominent racer but wide draw and stiff finish possible negatives.

RaceName: Tote Every Day Is A Money-Back Day Handicap
Spotlight: Progressive filly on a hat-trick of handicap wins, after successes over this trip at Fairyhouse and when defying 12lb rise at the Curragh, making all in beating her elders; up a further 11lb here but still greatly respected.

RaceName: Tote Every Day Is A Money-Back Day Handicap
Spotlight: Kingman filly didn't show much in sole start last season at Cork (7f, soft) when slowly away, but reappeared to land Gowran fillies' maiden last month, wearing down a front-runner late on over 1m (yielding) - third has won since; unexposed entering handicap ranks and booking of in-form claimer a positive.

RaceName: Tote Every Day Is A Money-Back Day Handicap
Spotlight: Enjoying a fine season with 1m wins in handicap at Cork, rated race at Leopardstown (Krasimir third) and most recently in Killarney handicap 16 days ago, defying top-weight narrowly; 5lb rise for latest but should remain competitive.

RaceName: Tote Every Day Is A Money-Back Day Handicap
Spotlight: Several placings before off the mark in Dundalk AW maiden over this trip earlier in the month under a positive ride, not needing to improve on previous turf efforts which included Leopardstown third (beaten 1l) to Johnny Soda whom he now meets on 8lb better terms; contender from a good draw.

RaceName: Tote Every Day Is A Money-Back Day Handicap
Spotlight: Progressive handicapper with wins this term at Limerick, Leopardstown and most recently at former venue last month, despite hanging right; later in month didn't count in Curragh premier handicap but claims back in grade here.

RaceName: Tote Every Day Is A Money-Back Day Handicap
Spotlight: Sprang a 33-1 surprise in a Leopardstown maiden this time last year (7f, good) but hasn't built on that effort, most recently seasonal return at same venue early this month (hanging left late on); entitled to come on for that.

RaceName: Tote Every Day Is A Money-Back Day Handicap
Spotlight: Maiden hasn't lived up to a quite lofty rating achieved on the back of Curragh maiden third last autumn (soft-to-heavy), although wasn't disgraced in Gowran conditions event in June; looks to have it to do off this mark.

RaceName: Tote Every Day Is A Money-Back Day Handicap
Spotlight: Newmarket debut winner for Charlie Appleby last summer (7f, good-to-firm); creditable yard debut in Musselburgh handicap in April but has taken a backward step both starts since.

RaceName: Tote Every Day Is A Money-Back Day Handicap
Spotlight: Placed in Dundalk AW maidens last winter, not so good there in May before successful hurdling debut in Limerick 3yo maiden early this month, despite taking keen hold and making most (good); didn't get home over 1m2f on sole Flat handicap effort (Navan) before that win so drop back in trip should suit.

RaceName: Tote Every Day Is A Money-Back Day Handicap
Spotlight: Dundalk AW maiden winner at this trip in April; behind Johnny Soda last two starts, most recently beaten 3l in Killarney handicap when never on terms over 1m; bit to find but stiffer track could suit.

Not at best on any of four starts since returned to turf in April, most recently when towards rear throughout at Newbury this month, but now 1lb lower than when dominating this race from the front a year ago; can't be ruled out.

OwnerName: Mr & Mrs Dowling And & Mrs Marney
Spotlight: Did not progress after last September's AW novice win but looked back in good nick when cosily exploiting much-reduced mark at Nottingham (1m2f, good to firm) this month; this race is much stronger but a 3lb rise ought to be manageable if she's in similar form again.

Came good at fifth attempt, at Redcar (1m2f, good) ten weeks ago; not seen since but the front pair drew clear in that race and she shaped as though this stiffer track might suit her better; high on the list.

Unexposed 3yo who made the frame in all three qualifying races, albeit a shade disappointing when well-held third of five over 1m last time; back up in trip for this handicap debut and probably still has potential.

OwnerName: Michael P Tudor & J P M O'Connor
Spotlight: Travelled well before asserting at Leicester (1m2f, good to firm) a fortnight ago, opening her account at the eighth attempt; contests a deeper race here but is only 3lb higher; ought to make her presence felt.
Gained all three wins on AW but was placed on turf here (1m, good) and at Windsor (1m2f, good to firm) on last two appearances; still unexposed over today's trip; likely contender again.

OwnerName: Hold My Beer, Gee Gees Racing & N Clark
Spotlight: Quite well handicapped if judged on this spring's placed form over 7f/1m and may not have been suited by the contours of Beverley when upped to 8.4f this month (still ran okay); has a fighting chance if stamina holds out over this even longer trip; tongue-tie added.
Caused 40-1 surprise off today's mark at Kempton (1m4f, AW) in April but has been below that form lately, including when last of seven in similar race to this over C&D on Thursday.

Six-race maiden; kept of for third when upped to 8.4f and fitted with cheekpieces at Beverley (good to firm) this month and looks worth a crack at this even longer trip but others in this field have more persuasive profiles.

Ended three-race 2yo campaign with 1m AW win in December and was close second when upped to 1m2f for this month's seasonal/handicap/turf debut at Salisbury (good to firm); has obvious scope to build upon that performance here and benefits from Ashley Lewis' useful 5lb claim; good chance.

Broke on terms for the first time and was able to dictate before showing good battling qualities to get back up at Hamilton 18 days ago; that was her first crack at a trip as far as 1m3f and some extra yardage here will suit even better; will likely encounter similar ground this evening; the one to beat off 3lb higher.

No real impact in 1m2f/1m3f handicaps following break/gelding operation then ran poorly in first-time headgear (blinkers) over 1m4f; less severe headgear goes on here and he'll likely encounter genuine fast ground for the first time.

OwnerName: J O'Mulloy And W R Muir
Spotlight: Front-runner; checked out quickly at Salisbury on Saturday but could easily bounce back given he left a poor run behind when turned out just nine days later earlier in the month.
Ran much better than in first two handicaps when upped significantly in trip to 1m5f at Ayr last time but he'll need to learn to settle if he's to see these kind of distances out.

RaceName: Bet With Tote.ie On Racing & Sports Handicap
OwnerName: Sarah Dale & Wayne Dale & Ian Foster
Spotlight: Three flat wins for Michael Bell came at 1m6f on quick ground; ordinary enough hurdles form for current yard but fine run on the flat over this trip at the Curragh on Derby weekend back on decent ground, only losing second late on when 2lb out of handicap; down in grade here and tongue-tie tried; has to be respected.

RaceName: Bet With Tote.ie On Racing & Sports Handicap
Spotlight: Successful yard debut on seasonal return at the Curragh in March (1m4f, heavy) and has run well on both turf starts since over same trip; stamina unproven over this far.

RaceName: Bet With Tote.ie On Racing & Sports Handicap
Spotlight: Both flat wins in 2024 came at Roscommon; generally below best in recent years, never sighted at the Curragh on fast ground latest; wide draw, hard to fancy.

RaceName: Bet With Tote.ie On Racing & Sports Handicap
Spotlight: Twice placed in juvenile hurdles but hasn't progressed, well below best in Bellewstown maiden latest; good run when last seen on the flat in Navan maiden (1m2f, soft) in April 2025 but questions to answer here in terms of trip on handicap debut.

RaceName: Bet With Tote.ie On Racing & Sports Handicap
Spotlight: Both flat wins have been at 1m4f, including Roscommon handicap last autumn off 73 (soft); reappeared last month, well held in both attempts over fences; opposable.

RaceName: Bet With Tote.ie On Racing & Sports Handicap
Spotlight: Very useful hurdler has come good on the flat of late on decent ground, winning Leopardstown maiden and following up in 2m1f Killarney handicap when allowed to dictate matters; up 7lb for that but can still go well.

RaceName: Bet With Tote.ie On Racing & Sports Handicap
Spotlight: Useful juvenile hurdler for James Owen in 2024-25 season; AW winner last year but never sighted on last month's flat return at Roscommon; visor replaces cheekpieces and bad draw so of limited appeal.

RaceName: Bet With Tote.ie On Racing & Sports Handicap
Spotlight: Useful hurdler who has won twice on the Flat, including here over 1m4f last October off 75; creditable effort at Gowran earlier in season but improvement needed on recent Limerick run.

RaceName: Bet With Tote.ie On Racing & Sports Handicap
Spotlight: Bumper and maiden hurdle winner for Harry Kelly; recent flat maiden efforts have been creditable but not sure if they justify this initial handicap mark and poorly drawn.

RaceName: Bet With Tote.ie On Racing & Sports Handicap
Spotlight: Hasn't added to Leopardstown 2yo success, placed over mid-distances in Britain last year; back from a break with tongue-tie tried but hard to make a convincing case for.

RaceName: Bet With Tote.ie On Racing & Sports Handicap
Spotlight: Dangerous when gets his favoured soft conditions, as when bolting up at Bellewstown in October; recent Ballinrobe comeback run should have brought him on but won't get his preferred ground here and terrible draw to overcome.

RaceName: Bet With Tote.ie On Racing & Sports Handicap
Spotlight: Three wins on the Flat include here over 1m6f three years ago; below best under both codes of late, fair bit to find with Gaoth Chuil on recent Killarney effort.

RaceName: Bet With Tote.ie On Racing & Sports Handicap
Spotlight: Was gaining a third career win when scoring over 1m4f at Tramore early this month, winning convincingly under a hold-up ride; hit with 11lb hike takes him to a career-high but in-form claimer takes off 7lb.

RaceName: Bet With Tote.ie On Racing & Sports Handicap
Spotlight: Won over just shy of this trip at Leopardstown last summer off 69; mainly campaigned over hurdles since; Killarney comeback run was over an inadequate trip so more expected here although cruel draw.

RaceName: Bet With Tote.ie On Racing & Sports Handicap
Spotlight: Twice a winner in Britain for James Ferguson at 1m4f; kept to hurdling so far by current trainer, just okay form; first try at this extended trip, okay mark.

RaceName: Bet With Tote.ie On Racing & Sports Handicap
Spotlight: Fairly useful hurdler last season, winning Roscommon maiden; well held in handicaps however, latest at same venue last month; standout flat run for Alan King when touched off in 1m6f Sandown handicap two years ago (Cock And Bull third); noteworthy jockey booking for flat return.

RaceName: Bet With Tote.ie On Racing & Sports Handicap
Spotlight: Lightly raced mare; good efforts in final two maidens for Joseph O'Brien in October 2024; soon beaten on return from long absence in 1m6f Fairyhouse handicap last June but entitled to come on for that and usual cheekpieces back on here.

RaceName: Bet With Tote.ie On Racing & Sports Handicap
Spotlight: Three flat wins for various trainers in Britain and off the mark over hurdles for current trainer in 2m3f Market Rasen maiden in late May (good); had earlier not looked a straightforward ride on occasions; has had a break since.

Off the mark at the fifth attempt when making all in first-time cheekpieces off 6lb lower at Chepstow (1m4f, good to firm) 26 days ago; has since left Andrew Balding (bought for 20,000gns) and this well-bred gelding steps up in trip for his stable debut.

Ran to a similar level in each of his first three starts (1m2f-1m4f) and he was reported to have been unsuited by the going when failing to beat a rival home on his handicap debut at Newmarket (1m4f, good; first-time blinkers; trainer's representative said he would prefer it slower) last month; steps up in trip with a bit better needed.

Progressive 3yo who made it 4-4 in handicaps and 2-2 on turf when winning by a neck at Newbury (13.5f, good to firm) 20 days ago, showing a fine attitude; now 5lb higher but there could still be more to come from this improver.

OwnerName: W G & A G Vestey, E Gerber And P Inglett
Spotlight: Ran well when upped to 1m4f at Thirsk (good) in May and has run to a similar level in both starts since, including when second of five at Doncaster (1m4f, good to firm; first-time cheekpieces) 11 days ago; claims if seeing out this longer trip.

RaceName: Nelson Panoramic Restaurant Dining Packages From Just £90 Handicap
Spotlight: Cheekpieces added to tongue-tie when making the frame in deeper contest over the extended mile at Beverley last time, dropped in from widest draw before unable to sustain a promising run once negotiating traffic problems; should be able to adopt a better track position this time.

RaceName: Nelson Panoramic Restaurant Dining Packages From Just £90 Handicap
Spotlight: Signed off for Charlie Johnston/kicked off for James Tate in winning form; last or second last in four starts for current connections (ridden forward each time) and can only be watched; goes without headgear.

RaceName: Nelson Panoramic Restaurant Dining Packages From Just £90 Handicap
Spotlight: Proved 50-1 win in five-runner Southwell maiden on second start to be no fluke when running well under a penalty at Haydock next time; overracing in both handicap starts proved terminal, particularly when attempting to see out 1m2f for the first time 59 days ago; change of jockey this evening.

RaceName: Nelson Panoramic Restaurant Dining Packages From Just £90 Handicap
Spotlight: Ready winner on debut at Ayr last August (7f) and bounced back from a couple of lesser efforts to be runner-up in first handicap this June (8.3f, Hamilton); second crack at 1m2f when beaten 6l into third at the scene of her win latest; that trip may want revisiting at some stage but she makes some appeal over 1m here.

RaceName: Nelson Panoramic Restaurant Dining Packages From Just £90 Handicap
Spotlight: Best effort for Brian Meehan came over 1m2f (managed second) and was last seen stretching out to 1m4f; changed hands for 14,000gns this month; this won't take much winning and a positive market move would look significant; goes without headgear.
